vendor_api_version: Slack Web API as documented on 2026-09-26

divergences.reason: upload_url points at the host the client called (/upload/v1/{file_id} on the app emulator, following X-Forwarded-Host behind the LocalStack gateway). Slack points it at files.slack.com.
divergences.operator_note: Operator-approved plan for WonderTwin-AI/wondertwin #325, 2026-10-01: the upload stays on the app emulator.

divergences.reason: An upload body over 10 MiB answers HTTP 413, the twincore request body cap. Slack's limit is not stated in the 2026-09-26 docs capture.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-01: log the gap (WonderTwin-AI/wondertwin #325). Raising the kit cap is a separate fleet decision.

divergences.reason: Any non-empty authorization code is accepted, once. The app emulator serves no slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize page, so no code is issued for the user's approval and none expires after ten minutes.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-02 (WonderTwin-AI/wondertwin #327): accept any non-empty code; the research Arazzo workflow takes the code as an input.

divergences.reason: The granted bot scopes are a fixed set (chat:write, channels:read, users:read), and token rotation is not served: tokens do not expire and grant_type=refresh_token answers invalid_refresh_token.
divergences.operator_note: Operator-approved plan for WonderTwin-AI/wondertwin #327, 2026-10-02.

divergences.reason: Any well-formed xoxb-, xoxp- or xapp- token is accepted as the default principal of its type, so two unseeded tokens of one type are the same caller. An xapp- app-level token is accepted on every Web API method and acts as the bot user; Slack accepts app-level tokens only on the few methods that take them. Slack answers invalid_auth for a token it did not issue.
divergences.operator_note: Operator-approved plan for WonderTwin-AI/wondertwin #321, 2026-10-01: tokens need not be seeded first.

divergences.reason: Scopes are not enforced: missing_scope is never returned and neither the x-oauth-scopes nor the x-accepted-oauth-scopes header is sent. users.identity answers only the identity.basic fields (the user's name and ID, and the workspace ID), as no identity.email, identity.avatar or identity.team scope is granted. So chat.postMessage and files.completeUploadExternal never answer not_in_channel: Slack refuses a post to a public channel the caller is not in unless the app has chat:write.public (chat.postMessage docs, Channel membership), and the app emulator lets any caller post to any channel.
divergences.operator_note: Deferred by the operator, 2026-10-01: scopes are PR 3b, after a refresh run captures the scope headers.

divergences.reason: trigger_id is not checked (never expired_trigger_id, exchanged_trigger_id or invalid_trigger_id) and the two-push limit is not enforced. The app emulator issues no triggers until interactivity is served.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-02 (WonderTwin-AI/wondertwin #326): open and push wait for Events and interactivity.

divergences.reason: Rate limits are not enforced: no method answers HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Calling a paginated method without pagination gets no stricter limit, and no rate tier is assigned to any method, so the docs and the Java SDK disagreeing on the tier of 24 methods has no effect.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-02: rate limits are not simulated in the community app emulator; simulating them likely belongs to the commercial emulator. This is a decision for Slack, not a standing rule for other app emulators.

divergences.reason: Every caller gets the documented page sizes: history defaults to 100 messages per call and replies to 1000, with no per-minute limit. Since 2025-05-29 Slack caps both methods at 15 messages per call, and one call per minute, for new commercially distributed apps not listed in the Slack Marketplace (changelog 2025-05-29). The app emulator answers as Slack does for an app the cap does not apply to, such as an internal or Marketplace app.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-07: declare, not simulate. The cap is a rate limit tied to commercial distribution, which the community app emulator does not simulate (see the rate-limit entry), and copying it would break paging in customers' tests.

divergences.route: Events API HTTP delivery and interactivity
divergences.reason: Events API HTTP delivery is served for five events: message from chat.postMessage, chat.meMessage (me_message), files.completeUploadExternal (file_share) and scheduled-message delivery, carrying the message's subtype, files and attachments as history holds them, message_deleted from chat.delete, reaction_added from reactions.add, member_joined_channel from conversations.join and conversations.invite, and member_left_channel from conversations.leave and conversations.kick. Each is signed and retried with x-slack-retry-num and x-slack-retry-reason, a failure answered with x-slack-no-retry: 1 is not retried, and setting a Request URL through POST /admin/events/config makes the url_verification handshake (--webhook-url at startup does not). The channel_type on member_joined_channel and member_left_channel, C for a public channel and G for a private one, is unverified because Slack's reference page for those events is not in the captured docs. Not served: the other events Slack sends for these writes (message_changed, the channel_join message, pin_added, channel and file events, app_mention and the rest), Socket Mode and interactivity payloads. too_many_redirects is never the retry reason, Delayed Events and the failure-rate disabling of subscriptions are not modelled, and every event goes to the configured Request URL whatever the app's subscriptions or channel membership. The retry schedule defaults to Slack's (nearly immediately, 1 minute, 5 minutes) and can be shortened through POST /admin/events/config.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-09-28 (research/twins/slack/mvp.md section 9): Events API HTTP delivery is in the MVP; Socket Mode, modals and agents stay deferred. Operator decision, 2026-10-06: fill gaps for anything Slack has not deprecated, so member events, url_verification and x-slack-no-retry are served; the events beyond the five served are follow-ups.

divergences.reason: Answers unknown_method before authentication. Slack sunset files.upload on 2025-11-12 (changelog 2025-03-17), but the 2026-09-26 unauthenticated probe (obs-004) shows Slack still routes the name to its auth check. Use files.getUploadURLExternal and files.completeUploadExternal.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-06: remove methods Slack has retired or degraded rather than serve or declare them.

divergences.reason: Answers unknown_method. Slack still serves these methods, but its July 2023 changelog ("It's later already for stars and reminders") calls them degraded or useless since Save it for Later replaced both features.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-06: remove methods Slack has retired or degraded rather than serve or declare them.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Removal of degraded methods; no vendor behaviour is reproduced or departed from beyond the method being absent.

divergences.route: POST /api/{method} for any method outside the supported use cases
divergences.reason: Answers unknown_method. Slack serves these methods; the app emulator supports only the methods its use cases need (research/twins/slack/mvp.md). Every Slack method marked recommended_scope deferred in research/twins/slack/method-inventory.json in WonderTwin-AI/wondertwin-docs is in this set, each with its revisit trigger in scope-recommendation.json. The 15 stubs the first build served for deferred methods (dialog.open, dnd.*, search.*, team.accessLogs, team.billableInfo, team.integrationLogs, team.profile.get, users.setPhoto, users.deletePhoto) were removed rather than kept as answers that looked real.
divergences.operator_note: Operator decision, 2026-10-06: state exactly what is supported; methods outside the supported use cases are not served and are declared once here instead of one entry per method.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: A scope boundary, not a departure from a documented or observed Slack behaviour.

divergences.reason: With a JSON body, query-string arguments are ignored. Slack's docs say not to mix a JSON body with query-string or form arguments ("Choose one approach per request", apis/web-api) but not how Slack answers a request that does. Mixing a query string with a form body is documented as allowed, and the app emulator merges the two.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: icon_url is accepted but not reflected on the message, because the captured references show no shape for it; username and icon_emoji are reflected. unfurl_links, unfurl_media and unfurl_app_links have no effect: the app emulator does not unfurl links.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Gaps in the captured references and in what the app emulator renders, not a recorded Slack quirk.

divergences.reason: There is no USLACK system user, and no system notifications are sent. Since 2026-06-17 Slack sends system notifications from USLACK rather than Slackbot.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: One app state is reproduced: a granular Slack app. Behaviour that Slack varies by app creation date or app type (research versioning.md section 2) is not modelled.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: Optional fields with no value are omitted from answers rather than set to null, following the official SDK fixtures, except where the docs show null: enterprise in the oauth.v2.access answer, and previous_view_id on a view. Whether live Slack omits or nulls each other field is unverified (the quirk is an inference awaiting a live capture).
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: Operator endpoints for seeding, inspecting and resetting state, and for fault injection. Slack has no equivalent. POST /admin/state replaces every store the body names, an empty one included, and keeps the stores it leaves out, so a seed file can name only what it fills; a snapshot taken from GET /admin/state names every store and restores the state exactly. POST /admin/reset empties every store and does not reload the --seed-file the emulator started with. POST /admin/webhooks/flush waits until every queued event is delivered or has used up its retries, so with a failing receiver and the default retry schedule it answers after about six minutes.
divergences.operator_note: Every app emulator serves the admin namespace.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: An app-emulator-only operator namespace; no vendor behaviour is involved.

divergences.reason: IDs, timestamps and cursors are shaped like Slack's but not identical. Generated IDs carry an underscore (C_000001, U_BOT, Bk_000001, S_000001), where Slack's are letters and digits only. A message ts is the second it was posted and a sequence number that counts up across the workspace as its fraction, not microseconds, so ts values are unique and ordered but the fraction does not read as a time. Cursors are opaque base64 that name the kind of list they page (channels, users, messages), so a cursor from one method can page another of the same kind.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: The token is read from an Authorization header with the scheme written Bearer; another spelling, such as bearer, answers invalid_auth. A token inside a JSON body is ignored, so a JSON call without the header answers not_authed. Slack's docs say a token in a JSON body is not accepted, but not which error Slack answers for either case.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: A multi-person message gets a C conversation ID, as public and newer private channels do. Slack has given multi-person messages G IDs, and its changelog tells apps not to rely on the first letter of a conversation ID.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: Only Home tab views are published. A profile view answers invalid_arguments; Slack publishes profile views too.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: The call is checked as the docs describe (the message, its channel, the links in its text and the unfurls format) and acknowledged, but the unfurl is not shown on the message. The app emulator sends no link_shared events, so any unfurl_id answers invalid_unfurl_id, and the domains an app may unfurl are not modelled, so cannot_find_service and cannot_unfurl_url are never returned.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Unfurl rendering and link_shared delivery are not captured in the references; no quirk records them.

divergences.reason: A scheduled message posts when post_at has passed on the app emulator's clock, at the next Web API or GET /admin/messages call, rather than at post_at itself. The limit of 30 messages scheduled to one channel within five minutes (restricted_too_many) is not enforced.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: state exactly what is and is not supported, and never claim what the app emulator does not do.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Delivery timing is a property of the emulator's lazy clock, not a documented Slack behaviour.

divergences.reason: An admin or owner may set another user's profile and an owner an admin's, without the paid-plan and data-source settings Slack also requires. A changed email takes effect at once; Slack updates it only after the user confirms by email. Only the documented non-custom fields and custom fields are set.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: state exactly what is and is not supported, and never claim what the app emulator does not do.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Workspace plan and email confirmation are outside the app emulator's single-workspace model.

divergences.reason: A file's url_private and url_private_download serve its bytes on the host the client called, to any call with a token the app emulator accepts. A call without one answers HTTP 403; how Slack's files host answers it is not in the references. Uploaded bytes are not kept in a state snapshot.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.

divergences.reason: emoji.list lists only seeded custom emoji, and include_categories adds no Unicode categories. team.info marks the default icon with image_default and serves no icon images, and bots.info serves no bot icons.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: state exactly what is and is not supported, and never claim what the app emulator does not do.

divergences.reason: Some of Slack's conversation checks and shapes are not reproduced. A channel name, or a user ID for a direct message, is not accepted as channel: only a conversation ID is. A private channel is answered as is_channel false and is_group true, the legacy group shape. exclude_archived is ignored by conversations.list and users.conversations. Private channel membership is not checked on conversations.info, history and members, so any caller can read them. conversations.invite does not require the caller to be a member (not_in_channel); conversations.create and rename check only that a name is given and not taken, not Slack's naming rules (invalid_name_specials and the rest); conversations.leave never answers cant_leave_general or last_member. users.getPresence answers active for a user that does not exist.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: state exactly what is and is not supported, and never claim what the app emulator does not do.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Documented checks and shapes the app emulator does not reproduce; no quirk records them.

divergences.reason: Some fields and options are not served. A thread parent carries no reply_count, reply_users or latest_reply, and a reply no parent_user_id. files.sharedPublicURL and files.revokePublicURL set is_public and permalink rather than public_url_shared and permalink_public; files carry no shares, groups or ims, and a file's permalink is https://files.slack.com/{team}/{file} rather than Slack's workspace URL. files.list lists files oldest first. reactions.list pages with cursor and limit, not count and page, and lists items oldest first. bookmarks.edit ignores emoji. usergroups.list ignores include_users and include_count, and usergroups.update ignores channels. A view's hash is drawn from the same sequence as message timestamps, so it is unique but uses up ts sequence numbers.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: state exactly what is and is not supported, and never claim what the app emulator does not do.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Undelivered fields and options of documented objects; no quirk records them.

divergences.route: POST /api/files.completeUploadExternal, usergroups.users.update, conversations.invite, conversations.mark, chat.postEphemeral, users.profile.set
divergences.reason: Some answers follow the documented error list where the docs do not say which error applies. Completing a file whose bytes never reached the upload URL answers file_not_found. usergroups.users.update naming a user outside the workspace answers failed_for_some_users. conversations.invite with force invites the valid users and answers ok without listing the ones it skipped. conversations.mark checks that ts is a timestamp, not that a message has it. chat.postEphemeral with no user answers user_not_found, and a user who does not exist is user_not_in_channel. users.profile.set sets a profile field given a value of the wrong type to empty rather than answering invalid_arguments. A scheduled message is given its ts when it is delivered, not post_at.
divergences.operator_note: Operator rule, 2026-10-06: where the captured references do not settle a behaviour, declare it rather than invent it.
divergences.no_quirk_reason: Error choices the captured docs leave open; no quirk records them.
